NUM	<p>8c4a_6d91</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f14;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #864f14;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f14;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0e6b6b;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0e6b6b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0e6b6b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7043a7;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7043a7;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7043a7;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bmp, +++, bmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795800;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7043a7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7043a7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #96401d;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #96401d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96401d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5db0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b5db0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4a690e;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4a690e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a690e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #19687a;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #19687a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #19687a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7043a7;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7043a7;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e333e;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9e333e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e333e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4fb4;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4f4fb4;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4f4fb4;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, deh, +++, deh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e333e;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0e6b6b;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0e6b6b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0e6b6b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4f4fb4;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4f4fb4;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype.
